extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners/staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing confidentiality, public access, national-security review, property-rights statements to DOE/NASA, third-party pre-issuance submissions, and foreign-filing licenses for U.S. patent applications. Guidance is aimed at handling requests for application information, preparing required statements, and obtaining or responding to foreign filing licenses and secrecy orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of patent applications (35 U.S.C. 122(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for patents shall be kept in confidence by the Patent and Trademark Office and no information concerning the same given without authority of the applicant or owner unless necessary to carry out the provisions of an Act of Congress or in such special circumstances as may be determined by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rule preserving confidentiality of unpublished applications; applies to status, subject matter, and access unless statutory/regulatory exceptions apply. Employees are legally obligated to preserve pending applications in confidence until published or patented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing of patent applications (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application for a patent shall be published promptly after the expiration of a period of 18 months from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought; applicant may request earlier publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director determines procedures for publication. Publication is subject to exceptions (e.g., nonpublication request). A Director determination whether to release information about a published application is final and nonreviewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to publication (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall not be published if it is no longer pending; is subject to a secrecy order under section 181; is a provisional application under 111(b); or is an application for a design patent under chapter 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these conditions apply, the application will not be published under the 18-month rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication request and foreign-filing certification (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant certifies upon filing that the invention has not and will not be the subject of an application filed in another country or under an international agreement that requires 18-month publication, the application shall not be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may rescind such request at any time. If applicant later files corresponding foreign/international application, applicant must notify the Director within 45 days or the U.S. application will be regarded as abandoned. If rescinded or notice given, the application will be published as soon as practical. Where foreign-filed applications are less extensive than the U.S. application, applicant may submit a redacted copy eliminating parts not contained in foreign filings; Director may publish only the redacted copy if received within 16 months after earliest effective filing date. Section 154(d) benefits do not apply to a claim if the redacted description does not enable a skilled person to make and use the claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party preissuance submissions (35 U.S.C. 122(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any third party may submit for consideration any patent, published patent application, or other printed publication of potential relevance to examination, if submission is made in writing before the earlier of (A) notice of allowance, or (B) the later of (i) 6 months after publication, or (ii) date of first rejection under 35 U.S.C. 132 of any claim by the examiner during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must (A) set forth a concise description of the asserted relevance of each submitted document; (B) be accompanied by such fee as the Director may prescribe; and (C) include a statement by the submitter affirming compliance with the section. Timeliness and required content are strict; failure to satisfy requirements may render the submission ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Files open to public for published applications (37 CFR 1.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification, drawings, and all papers relating to the file of a published application, a patent, or a statutory invention registration are open to inspection by the public, and copies may be obtained upon payment of fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application was published in redacted form pursuant to § 1.217, the complete file wrapper and contents will not be available if redaction requirements have been met and the application is still pending. Fees for copies per § 1.19(b)(2) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent applications preserved in confidence (37 CFR 1.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that have not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) are generally preserved in confidence and information concerning filing, pendency, subject matter, including status information and access, will only be given as set forth in §1.11 or §1.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory foundation for the confidentiality rule; cross-references indicate limited exceptions and procedures for disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories when application records may be available to public (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(i)-(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Records associated with patent applications may be available in specified situations: (i) patented applications/statutory invention registrations; (ii) published abandoned applications; (iii) published pending applications; (iv) unpublished abandoned applications that are identified or relied upon; (v) unpublished pending applications whose benefit is claimed; (vi) unpublished pending applications incorporated by reference or otherwise identified; (vii) when a petition for access or a power to inspect is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category has its own conditions and procedures (e.g., written request, payment of fees, identification criteria). For unpublished files, availability often depends on identification in another published document or benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c). Access to paper file of pending applications is normally not provided except under narrow exceptions (paragraphs (c) or (i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status information that may be communicated to the public (37 CFR 1.14(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Status information means only: (A) whether the application is pending, abandoned, or patented; (B) whether the application has been published; (C) the application number or the serial number plus any one of the filing date of the national application, the international filing date or the date of entry into the national stage; and (D) whether another application claims the benefit of the application and related status information for those applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status information may be accessed via Patent Center or Private PAIR. Other details (e.g., filing date of abandonment, whether CIP/continuation/divisional) may be confidential and not provided to the public in many circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee obligations and handling of physical/electronic files
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPTO employees are legally obligated to preserve pending applications in confidence; employees having custody must maintain conformity with law; no part of any application should be reproduced or copied except for official purposes; files must not be displayed or handled to permit perusal by unauthorized public; non-electronic files removed from operating area must have proper charge on Patent Data Portal; do not place official papers in unsecured locations; interoffice mail must be appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply may lead to suspension, removal, or criminal penalties. Take corrective action for IFW messages with faulty identifications or incorrect routing immediately. Examiners/classifiers assisting public searchers must ensure confidentiality of information revealed by searchers (see MPEP §1701). Avoid inadvertent disclosure of filing dates or application numbers in Office actions or file notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone and in-person verification procedure for unpublished pending/abandoned applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When handling incoming telephone or in-person requests concerning an unpublished pending or abandoned application, no information should be disclosed until the requester's identity is adequately verified. Obtain caller’s full name, application number, telephone number, and whether a patent practitioner of record exists; verify as set forth; call back appropriate verified telephone number before releasing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent practitioner is of record, ask for registration number and call practitioner’s telephone number from Patent Data Portal. If no practitioner, ask why entitled to information and verify correspondence address of record; if association cannot be verified, no information released. For in-person requests, verify identification similarly before releasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification steps using Patent Data Portal
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Patent Data Portal to verify registration number or correspondence address, obtain telephone numbers of patent practitioners of record, and to determine whether a patent practitioner is of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return the call using the telephone number obtained from Patent Data Portal; release information only to the verified practitioner or verified requester. Patent Data Portal is the authoritative source for status/location information for Office personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is entitled to status information without additional written authority (37 CFR 1.14(c) and MPEP §104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized requesters entitled to status information: (1) the applicant; (2) a patent practitioner of record; (3) the assignee or an assignee of an undivided part interest; (4) the inventor or a joint inventor; or (5) a registered attorney or agent named in papers accompanying the application or national stage documents if a power of attorney has not been appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requester is one of these, or has written authority signed by one of them, they are entitled to status information. AAU (Application Assistance Unit) determines entitlement for pre-examination/post-examination processing and can be contacted for assistance. Written authority formats and who may sign are discussed elsewhere in MPEP §104.

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage/international publication status inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: If requester is not in the authorized categories but the application is a national stage application or claims benefit of a published international application where the U.S. was designated, requester is entitled to status information for the national stage application and any applications claiming benefit of the published international application upon submission of the first page of the published international application or PCT Gazette page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status request should be made in writing to International Patent Legal Administration. For national stage applications only limited status (serial number/filing date and pending/abandoned/patented) may be given; other continuity data may remain confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: International design application inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: For international design applications maintained by the Office as a designated office for national processing or in capacity as office of indirect filing, status information may be made available where contained in the file of the international design application maintained by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar procedures as for international utility/national stage applications – provide required documentation and direct inquiries to relevant help desks (PCT Help desk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy orders and national security (35 U.S.C. 181/Chapter 17 references)
rubrics_metrics.description: No application shall be published if publication or disclosure would be detrimental to national security. The Director shall establish procedures to ensure such applications are promptly identified and secrecy maintained in accordance with chapter 17; secrecy orders may be imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications identified as national security sensitive are handled under Secrecy Orders with special handling and nonpublication. If a Secrecy Order is issued, its restrictions must be immediately observed. Secrecy Orders may also prompt referral to defense agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting inventions to DOE (42 U.S.C. 2182 provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications appearing to disclose inventions relating to atomic energy are reported to the Department of Energy, which will be given access to the applications. Reporting does not constitute a determination that the subject matter is in fact useful or an invention specified by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property rights statements to DOE may be solicited informally (45-day letter) and updated if necessary; provisional applications are not subject to DOE/NASA review. If a proper statement is not received after requests, a formal statutory request with a 30-day response period is issued; failure to respond properly and timely will result in abandonment of the application (subject to revival provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Property rights statements to DOE and NASA — content and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The law requires the statement to set forth 'the full facts' surrounding the conception and making of the invention; statements must be in oath or declaration form and signed by the inventor(s), assignee, obligated assignee, or other person with sufficient proprietary interest. Form paragraphs or broad generalized statements are not ordinarily sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant lacks firsthand knowledge, the statement should identify the source of information or be accompanied by supplemental declarations by persons with requisite knowledge. Substitute statements may be accepted (e.g., assignee officer) when inventor is deceased/unavailable after diligent efforts. Statements should be accurate to the facts at time submitted and updated if necessary at allowance. Sample acceptable formats are provided in MPEP. Willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and may jeopardize validity of the application/patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and processing of DOE/NASA property-rights statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal requests (45-day letter) may be sent shortly after filing to applicants whose nonprovisional applications are flagged by USPTO security screeners; response within 45 days expedites processing. If defective, applicant is given opportunity to correct during informal period; if no response or cooperation, a formal 30-day statutory request will be made and failure to timely respond results in abandonment (revivable under 37 CFR 1.137).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications are not subject. Applicants should promptly file supplemental statements if inventorship is corrected during pendency (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.48).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for property-rights statements — specifics to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements should set forth full facts unique to the invention and include who made/conceived the invention, dates, employment relationship (if made during employment), use of employer facilities/funds, other relevant facts; provide sworn declarations or oaths signed by all inventors where no government funds/considerations were involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP provides an acceptable sample declaration that includes sections for (I) inventors employed by an organization, (II) self-employed inventors, (III) statements that invention was not made under Atomic Energy Commission/DOE contract, and (IV) statements about relation to NASA contracts. The sample emphasizes accuracy and legal penalties for false statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filing license requirements and petitions (37 CFR 5.x references)
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign filing license is required for certain filings abroad; petitions for licenses (e.g., under 37 CFR 5.12(b), 5.14, 5.25) should be filed with Licensing and Review and processed by Office of Petitions. Petitions may be relevant when filing receipt license is not granted, filing receipt not yet issued, no corresponding U.S. application exists, subject matter additional to licensed matter is sought, or expedited handling is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of any license is indicated on the license. Applicants are encouraged to hand-deliver or fax license requests directly to Licensing and Review and provide contact/fax numbers for prompt delivery. Licenses generally granted within 3 business days if no national security concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive foreign filing licenses (37 CFR 5.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for a retroactive filing license may be filed under 37 CFR 5.25 if an unlicensed foreign filing has occurred; requirements include specifying countries, actual dates of filing, establishing nature of the error for each act of proscribed foreign filing, and a verified statement in oath or declaration form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licenses under 37 CFR 5.25 are retroactive only for specific acts of foreign filing. For petitions filed prior to Sept. 16, 2012, additional requirements (e.g., specifying that error occurred without deceptive intent) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of foreign filing licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon written notification from the USPTO, any foreign filing license required by 37 CFR 5.11(a) may be revoked. Revocation ordinarily indicates need for referral to defense agencies; revocation is effective on date notice is mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation of a filing receipt license does not necessarily preclude narrower-scope licenses under 37 CFR 5.12(b). Foreign filings that occurred prior to revocation need not be abandoned, but additional filings without a license are not permitted unless six months have elapsed from the filing of any corresponding U.S. application. If a Secrecy Order is imposed, its restrictions must be observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for failing to obtain necessary foreign filing license (35 U.S.C. 182,185,186)
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties include loss of patenting rights in addition to possible fine or imprisonment; petitions for retroactive licenses are processed by Licensing and Review and decided by Office of Petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to obtain required licenses can have severe civil and criminal consequences; applicants should seek licenses promptly and follow petition procedures if unlicensed filings occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection and referral of improper foreign filings by examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner learns of a corresponding foreign application filed before the U.S. application had been on file for six months and the invention appears to have been made in the U.S., the examiner shall refer the application to Licensing and Review calling attention to the foreign application. Pending investigation, the application may be returned to the Technology Center for prosecution on the merits; when otherwise in condition for allowance, the application will be resubmitted to Licensing and Review unless Licensing and Review already reported no bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should follow referral procedures; Licensing and Review may request transfer of the application if actions under 35 U.S.C. 185 are necessary. Examiners must note foreign filing dates and coordinate with Licensing and Review for potential penalties or remedial steps.
